vertical-premium.title: The Vertical Premium: Height and Housing Prices
vertical-premium.overview:
Research Question

How does the relative height of a property from flood elevation affect housing prices? This study examines the "vertical premium" - the additional value homebuyers place on properties situated higher above potential flood levels.

💡 Key Finding: Properties located higher above flood elevation command significant price premiums of approximately 2-3% per meter, even after controlling for other factors. This effect amplified dramatically after the 2013 Calgary flood.

Peak Flood Duration

The research analyzes one of Canada's costliest natural disasters, which provides a unique natural experiment to understand how actual flood experience influences housing market behavior.

Methodology

  • Data Source: Calgary residential property transactions combined with detailed flood elevation maps
  • Analysis Period: Pre-flood (2010-2013) and post-flood (2013-2016) comparison
  • Key Variable: Vertical distance (meters) from property to flood elevation line
  • Statistical Approach: Hedonic pricing model with spatial controls and temporal comparison
  • Sample Size: Over 50,000 residential property transactions

Key Results

  1. Vertical Premium Exists: Each additional meter above flood elevation adds approximately 2-3% to property value, controlling for other property characteristics
  2. Post-Flood Amplification: The premium increased significantly after the 2013 flood event, with properties 10m+ above flood elevation showing nearly 19% premium
  3. Spatial Variation: Effects are strongest in areas with direct flood experience and diminish with distance from flooded areas
  4. Market Capitalization: The housing market rapidly incorporated flood risk information, with premiums appearing within months of the disaster

Implications

🏙️ For Urban Planning

  • Prioritize flood mitigation investments in high-value areas
  • Inform zoning and development policies in flood-prone regions
  • Design equitable disaster recovery strategies
  • Better understand market-based risk valuation

🏡 For Homeowners & Investors

  • Quantify flood risk impact on property values
  • Make informed home purchase decisions
  • Evaluate elevation-based protection investments
  • Develop better insurance strategies

🎯 Innovation

This research introduces the concept of "vertical premium" as a distinct component of housing value, separate from traditional flood plain designations. Unlike binary flood zone classifications (in/out), it captures the continuous relationship between elevation and value, providing a more nuanced understanding of flood risk capitalization in housing markets.

mental-health-covid.title: Mental Health and COVID-19: The Role of Walkable Built Environment
mental-health-covid.overview:
Research Question

How did the COVID-19 pandemic affect mental health facility visits, and what role did the walkable built environment play in supporting mental health during this crisis?

💡 Key Finding: Neighborhoods with better walkability showed smaller declines in mental health facility visits during COVID-19. Access to walkable environments acted as a protective factor for mental health during the pandemic.

Study Period
Study Location

The COVID-19 pandemic led to unprecedented levels of mental health challenges, with anxiety and depression rates soaring globally. This study examines how built environment features influenced mental health service utilization during this critical period.

Methodology

  • Data Source: Mental health facility visit records linked with built environment measurements
  • Walkability Measures: Street connectivity, pedestrian infrastructure, mixed land use, and access to amenities
  • Analysis Period: Before and during COVID-19 pandemic (2019-2021)
  • Statistical Approach: Difference-in-differences analysis controlling for socioeconomic factors
  • Sample: Metropolitan Atlanta area neighborhoods

Key Results

  1. Walkability as Protective Factor: Neighborhoods with higher walkability scores experienced smaller decreases in mental health facility visits during the pandemic
  2. Access to Nature: Proximity to parks and green spaces was particularly important during lockdown periods
  3. Pedestrian Infrastructure: Presence of sidewalks and safe walking routes correlated with maintained mental health service access
  4. Equity Implications: The protective effect of walkability was stronger in lower-income neighborhoods, highlighting environmental justice dimensions

Implications

🏥 For Public Health

  • Integrate built environment planning into mental health strategies
  • Prioritize walkability improvements in pandemic preparedness
  • Recognize outdoor spaces as critical health infrastructure
  • Design interventions that leverage environmental factors

🏙️ For Urban Planning

  • Invest in walkable infrastructure as health resilience strategy
  • Ensure equitable distribution of walkable neighborhoods
  • Maintain pedestrian access during public health emergencies
  • Integrate health outcomes into walkability planning

🎯 Innovation

This research is among the first to quantitatively demonstrate the mental health benefits of walkable environments during a pandemic. It provides evidence that urban design decisions have direct implications for population mental health resilience in times of crisis.

urban-trees-safety.title: Urban Trees and Neighborhood Safety: The Role of Upkeep
urban-trees-safety.overview:
Research Question

Do urban trees make neighborhoods feel safer or more dangerous? This study examines the nuanced relationship between street trees and perceived safety, revealing that neighborhood upkeep matters more than tree presence alone.

💡 Key Finding: Trees increase perceived safety in well-maintained neighborhoods but can decrease safety perceptions in poorly maintained areas. The key is not just greening, but combining trees with good maintenance.

Study Location
Data Collection Method

Urban forestry has long faced a paradox: some research suggests trees increase safety through natural surveillance and community engagement, while other studies find trees create hiding spots and reduce visibility. This study resolves this paradox by examining the moderating role of neighborhood upkeep.

Methodology

  • Data Source: Google Street View images analyzed using computer vision for tree characteristics and maintenance indicators
  • Perceived Safety: Systematic social observation (SSO) ratings from trained observers
  • Tree Metrics: Canopy coverage, tree density, species diversity, and tree health
  • Maintenance Indicators: Sidewalk condition, building upkeep, litter presence, graffiti
  • Analysis: Multi-level regression models with interaction terms

Key Results

  1. Context-Dependent Effects: The relationship between trees and safety perception depends entirely on neighborhood maintenance levels
  2. Well-Maintained Areas: Trees significantly increase perceived safety (+15% improvement in safety scores)
  3. Poorly Maintained Areas: Trees decrease perceived safety (-8% reduction in safety scores)
  4. Tree Health Matters: Healthy, well-pruned trees have stronger positive effects than overgrown or dying trees
  5. Threshold Effect: Moderate tree coverage (30-50%) provides optimal safety benefits in maintained neighborhoods

Implications

🌳 For Urban Forestry

  • Tree planting must be coupled with maintenance programs
  • Regular pruning and tree care essential for safety benefits
  • Focus on tree health, not just tree quantity
  • Consider maintenance capacity before large-scale planting

🏘️ For Neighborhood Development

  • Invest in both greening and upkeep simultaneously
  • Address maintenance issues before adding trees
  • Engage communities in tree care programs
  • Design for long-term maintenance sustainability

🎯 Innovation

This research challenges the simple narrative of "trees = safety" by revealing the critical moderating role of neighborhood upkeep. It demonstrates that environmental interventions must consider contextual factors to be effective, advancing more nuanced approaches to urban greening.

streetscapes-servicescapes.title: Streetscapes as Servicescapes: Walkability and Business Attractiveness
streetscapes-servicescapes.overview:
Research Question연구 질문

Can improving streetscape walkability make local businesses more attractive to customers? This study explores whether pedestrian-friendly street design acts as part of the overall servicescape that influences consumer behavior.가로환경의 보행성 개선이 지역 상점을 고객에게 더 매력적으로 만들 수 있는가? 이 연구는 보행 친화적 가로 설계가 소비자 행동에 영향을 미치는 전체 서비스스케이프의 일부로 작용하는지를 탐구합니다.

💡 Key Finding:핵심 발견: Walkable streetscapes significantly increase business attractiveness, with effects comparable to traditional servicescape elements like interior design. A one-unit increase in walkability corresponds to a 12% increase in customer ratings.보행 친화적 가로환경이 비즈니스 매력도를 크게 증가시키며, 그 효과는 인테리어 디자인과 같은 전통적인 서비스스케이프 요소에 필적합니다. 보행성 1단위 증가는 고객 평가의 12% 증가에 해당합니다.

Study Area
Business Categories

Servicescape theory traditionally focuses on interior environments (lighting, layout, décor). This research extends the concept to include exterior streetscapes, arguing that the pedestrian experience approaching a business is part of the overall service environment.서비스스케이프 이론은 전통적으로 내부 환경(조명, 레이아웃, 장식)에 초점을 맞춥니다. 이 연구는 개념을 확장하여 외부 가로환경을 포함하며, 비즈니스에 접근하는 보행자 경험이 전체 서비스 환경의 일부임을 주장합니다.

Methodology연구 방법

  • Walkability Assessment: Automated audit using Google Street View images with deep learning to measure sidewalk quality, street trees, building transparency, and pedestrian amenities
  • Business Attractiveness: Yelp ratings and review sentiment analysis
  • Controls: Business type, price level, parking availability, transit access, neighborhood characteristics
  • Sample: Restaurants, cafes, retail shops, and service businesses
  • Analysis: Hierarchical models accounting for spatial clustering

Key Results주요 결과

  1. Significant Walkability Effect: Streetscape walkability independently predicts business attractiveness beyond traditional factors
  2. Stronger for Experience Businesses: Effects most pronounced for restaurants and cafes where customer experience is central
  3. Synergy with Traditional Servicescape: Good interior servicescape enhanced by good exterior streetscape (multiplicative effect)
  4. Pedestrian Infrastructure Matters: Presence of wide sidewalks, street furniture, and crossing amenities particularly important
  5. Return Visit Intentions: Walkable locations show higher rates of repeat customers based on review analysis

Implications시사점

🏪 For Business Owners

  • Consider streetscape quality in location decisions
  • Advocate for streetscape improvements near businesses
  • Invest in sidewalk-facing amenities (outdoor seating, displays)
  • Recognize walkability as competitive advantage

🏗️ For Urban Development

  • Streetscape improvements support local business vitality
  • Economic development and walkability are complementary
  • Pedestrian infrastructure has measurable ROI for commercial districts
  • Design streets with business attractiveness in mind

🎯 Innovation혁신성

This research introduces "streetscape as servicescape" concept, expanding our understanding of how physical environments influence consumer behavior. It provides quantitative evidence that urban design is not just aesthetic but economically consequential for local businesses.이 연구는 "서비스스케이프로서의 가로환경" 개념을 도입하여 물리적 환경이 소비자 행동에 미치는 영향에 대한 이해를 확장합니다. 도시 설계가 단순히 심미적일 뿐만 아니라 지역 비즈니스에 경제적으로 중요하다는 정량적 증거를 제공합니다.

environmental-equity-atlanta.title: Environmental Equity: Urban Tree Canopy Patterns in Atlanta
environmental-equity-atlanta.overview:
Research Question연구 질문

Are urban trees distributed equitably across different socioeconomic groups? This longitudinal study examines environmental justice in Atlanta's tree canopy distribution over two decades, revealing patterns of green inequality.도시 녹지가 사회경제적 그룹 간에 공평하게 분포되어 있는가? 이 종단 연구는 20년에 걸친 애틀랜타의 수목 피복 분포를 통해 환경 정의를 검토하고 녹지 불평등 패턴을 밝힙니다.

💡 Key Finding:핵심 발견: Significant disparities exist in tree canopy distribution. Low-income and minority neighborhoods have 15-20% less tree coverage than affluent areas, and these gaps have widened over time despite overall canopy growth.수목 피복 분포에 상당한 격차가 존재합니다. 저소득층 및 소수민족 거주 지역은 부유한 지역보다 15-20% 적은 수목 피복을 가지며, 전체 피복이 증가했음에도 불구하고 이러한 격차는 시간이 지남에 따라 확대되었습니다.

Temporal Analysis
Study Region

Urban trees provide numerous benefits including cooling, air quality improvement, and health benefits. However, these benefits may be inequitably distributed. This study uses remote sensing data to track tree canopy changes across Atlanta's diverse neighborhoods over nearly two decades.도시 수목은 냉각, 대기질 개선, 건강 증진 등 다양한 혜택을 제공합니다. 그러나 이러한 혜택이 불공평하게 분배될 수 있습니다. 이 연구는 원격 감지 데이터를 사용하여 약 20년에 걸쳐 애틀랜타의 다양한 지역에서 수목 피복 변화를 추적합니다.

Methodology연구 방법

  • Tree Canopy Data: High-resolution aerial imagery and LiDAR analysis for 1996, 2008, and 2014
  • Demographic Data: Census tract-level income, race/ethnicity, education, and housing characteristics
  • Temporal Analysis: Change detection algorithms to track canopy gain and loss
  • Statistical Methods: Spatial regression models accounting for neighborhood characteristics and urban development patterns
  • Equity Metrics: Gini coefficients and concentration curves for distributional analysis

Key Results주요 결과

  1. Persistent Inequality: Tree canopy coverage positively correlates with income and education levels across all time periods
  2. Widening Gap: Despite 5% overall canopy increase, disparities between high and low-income areas grew from 12% to 18%
  3. Racial Disparities: Predominantly Black neighborhoods have 20% less canopy than predominantly white neighborhoods with similar income levels
  4. Development Patterns: New development in affluent areas preserves more trees than development in lower-income areas
  5. Loss and Gain Patterns: Low-income areas experience more tree loss and less tree planting/regrowth

Implications시사점

🌲 For Urban Forestry Policy

  • Target tree planting programs to underserved neighborhoods
  • Provide resources for tree maintenance in low-income areas
  • Protect existing trees in vulnerable neighborhoods
  • Monitor equity metrics in urban forestry plans

⚖️ For Environmental Justice

  • Recognize tree canopy as environmental justice issue
  • Address structural factors behind green inequality
  • Ensure equitable distribution of climate adaptation resources
  • Engage communities in urban greening decisions

🎯 Innovation혁신성

This research provides longitudinal evidence of environmental inequity in urban tree distribution, moving beyond cross-sectional snapshots. It demonstrates that without intentional equity-focused interventions, green inequality can worsen even as overall canopy increases, informing more just urban forestry approaches.이 연구는 도시 수목 분포의 환경 불평등에 대한 종단적 증거를 제공하며, 단면적 스냅샷을 넘어섭니다. 의도적인 형평성 중심 개입이 없으면 전체 피복이 증가하더라도 녹지 불평등이 악화될 수 있음을 보여주며, 보다 공정한 도시 산림 접근 방식을 제시합니다.

audio-sensors-pedestrian.title: Audio-Based Sensors for Understanding Pedestrian Movement
audio-sensors-pedestrian.overview:
Research Question

Can audio sensors provide a novel, privacy-preserving way to understand pedestrian movement patterns? This study explores machine learning to detect pedestrian activity using sound instead of visual data.

💡 Key Finding: Audio sensors achieve 85%+ accuracy in detecting pedestrians while preserving privacy - a scalable alternative to video surveillance.

Preserving
Analysis Method

Audio sensors capture movement patterns without identifying individuals, addressing surveillance concerns in public spaces.

Methodology

  • Audio Collection: Sensors in various urban settings
  • Machine Learning: Deep learning to distinguish pedestrian sounds
  • Validation: Compared with manual observation

Key Results

  1. High Accuracy: 85%+ detection rate
  2. Privacy Safe: Cannot identify individuals
  3. Cost-Effective: Cheaper than cameras

Implications

Enables privacy-preserving pedestrian monitoring for urban planning and smart city applications.

🎯 Innovation

Pioneers audio-based pedestrian sensing as ethical alternative to visual surveillance.

asped-dataset.title: ASPED: Audio Dataset for Pedestrian Detection
asped-dataset.overview:
Research Question

How to create a comprehensive audio dataset for training ML models to detect pedestrians? ASPED is the first large-scale audio dataset for pedestrian detection.

💡 Key Finding: ASPED provides 100+ hours of labeled audio across diverse urban environments, enabling unprecedented pedestrian detection research.

Data Sources
Public Access

No comprehensive audio dataset existed for pedestrian detection. ASPED fills this gap with carefully labeled, diverse samples.

Methodology

  • Collection: Recorded in various urban settings
  • Labeling: Rigorous annotation for pedestrian presence and activity
  • Quality Control: Multi-rater validation (>90% agreement)

Key Results

  1. Scale: 100+ hours of labeled data
  2. Diversity: Multiple cities, times, contexts
  3. Open Access: Publicly available for research

Implications

Enables ML research in privacy-preserving urban sensing and smart city applications.

🎯 Innovation

First comprehensive public audio dataset for pedestrian detection research.

tree-crime-austin.title: Trees and Crime: Evidence from Austin
tree-crime-austin.overview:
Research Question

How do tree characteristics (species, size, canopy) relate to street crime? This study examines specific tree attributes beyond simple presence.

💡 Key Finding: Tree effects are highly nuanced. Large trees reduce some crimes but may increase others. Tree species and placement matter more than presence alone.

Data Period
Crime Categories

Environmental criminology suggests vegetation affects crime through visibility. This study examines how tree characteristics influence different crime types.

Methodology

  • Crime Data: Geocoded police records
  • Tree Inventory: Species, size, canopy data
  • Analysis: Street-segment level regression

Key Results

  1. Size Matters: Large trees reduce property crime
  2. Canopy Density: Dense canopy reduces daytime crime
  3. Species Variation: Deciduous vs evergreen show different patterns

Implications

Strategic tree planting considering crime prevention alongside environmental benefits.

🎯 Innovation

Demonstrates tree characteristics matter beyond simple presence for crime prevention.

microscale-macroscale-streetscapes.title: Integrating Microscale and Macroscale Urban Form
microscale-macroscale-streetscapes.overview:
Research Question연구 질문

Can microscale streetscapes enhance benefits of macroscale urban form? This examines whether street-level design amplifies neighborhood walkability.미시적 가로환경이 거시적 도시형태의 이점을 증진시킬 수 있는가? 가로 수준의 설계가 근린의 보행성을 증폭시키는지를 검토합니다.

💡 Key Finding:핵심 발견: Microscale quality significantly moderates macroscale effects. Good macro form with poor streetscapes shows 40% less benefit.미시적 품질이 거시적 효과를 크게 조절합니다. 좋은 거시적 형태라도 열악한 가로환경과 결합되면 40% 낮은 효과를 보입니다.

Microscale Data
Macroscale Data

Urban design operates at multiple scales. This research integrates macro (density, connectivity) and micro (sidewalks, facades) levels.도시 설계는 여러 규모에서 작동합니다. 이 연구는 거시적 수준(밀도, 연결성)과 미시적 수준(보도, 건물 외관)을 통합합니다.

Methodology연구 방법

  • Macroscale: Density, land use mix, connectivity
  • Microscale: Automated audit of Street View images
  • Analysis: Interaction models testing moderating effects

Key Results주요 결과

  1. Synergistic Effects: Benefits multiply when both scales are good
  2. Threshold: Poor microscale limits macroscale benefits
  3. Sidewalks Critical: Quality most important micro factor

Implications시사점

Require microscale design quality, not just macroscale density in development policy.개발 정책에서 거시적 밀도뿐만 아니라 미시적 설계 품질을 요구해야 합니다.

🎯 Innovation혁신성

Scale integration is critical - neither alone is sufficient for walkability.규모 통합이 필수적입니다 - 어느 하나만으로는 보행성에 충분하지 않습니다.

automated-walkability-audit.title: Automated Microscale Walkability Audit Method
automated-walkability-audit.overview:
Research Question연구 질문

Can we automate walkability audits using computer vision? This develops a method replacing costly manual audits with scalable automated assessment.컴퓨터 비전을 활용하여 보행환경 평가를 자동화할 수 있는가? 비용이 많이 드는 수작업 평가를 확장 가능한 자동 평가로 대체하는 방법을 개발합니다.

💡 Key Finding:핵심 발견: Automated audit achieves 90%+ agreement with expert audits while reducing costs by 95% and enabling city-wide analysis.자동화된 평가 방법이 전문가 평가와 90% 이상 일치하며, 비용은 95% 절감하고 도시 전체 분석을 가능하게 합니다.

Cost Reduction
Scalability

Traditional audits are expensive and not scalable. Computer vision offers automation using street-level imagery.전통적인 평가는 비용이 많이 들고 확장이 어렵습니다. 컴퓨터 비전은 가로 이미지를 활용한 자동화를 제공합니다.

Methodology연구 방법

  • Baseline: Expert manual audits
  • Automation: Deep learning on Street View images
  • Validation: Compared automated vs manual scores

Key Results주요 결과

  1. High Validity: 90%+ agreement with manual audits
  2. Cost Efficient: 95% cost reduction
  3. Scalable: Entire cities in hours vs months

Implications시사점

Enables comprehensive walkability assessment at city scale for planning and research.도시 전체 규모의 포괄적인 보행환경 평가를 계획 및 연구에 활용할 수 있습니다.

🎯 Innovation혁신성

Validates automated walkability assessment as viable alternative to manual audits.자동화된 보행환경 평가가 수작업 평가의 실용적 대안임을 검증합니다.

walkability-walking-behaviors.title: Walkability Factors and Walking Behaviors
walkability-walking-behaviors.overview:
Research Question연구 질문

Which walkability factors most predict walking behavior? This uses big data to disentangle effects of different environmental features.어떤 보행환경 요소가 보행 행태를 가장 잘 예측하는가? 빅데이터를 활용하여 다양한 환경 특성의 효과를 분리하여 분석합니다.

💡 Key Finding:핵심 발견: Street-level features predict walking as strongly as neighborhood factors, challenging macro-only approaches.가로 수준의 특성이 근린 수준 요소만큼 보행을 강력하게 예측하며, 거시적 접근만으로는 충분하지 않음을 보여줍니다.

Features Analyzed
Outcome Measure

Most research focuses on neighborhood-scale features. Street view and computer vision enable street-level analysis at scale.대부분의 연구는 근린 규모 특성에 초점을 맞춥니다. 스트리트뷰와 컴퓨터 비전을 통해 가로 수준의 대규모 분석이 가능합니다.

Methodology연구 방법

  • Behavior: Travel survey and pedestrian sensors
  • Environment: Multi-scale features from GIS and Street View
  • Analysis: Multi-level models separating scale effects

Key Results주요 결과

  1. Street-Level Critical: Explains 35-40% of variance
  2. Sidewalks: Width and condition strongest predictor
  3. Trees: Independently predict walking frequency

Implications시사점

Invest in street-level improvements, not just neighborhood form for walkability.보행성 향상을 위해 근린 형태뿐만 아니라 가로 수준 개선에 투자해야 합니다.

🎯 Innovation혁신성

Street-level experience as important as neighborhood form for walking.보행을 위해서는 가로 수준 경험이 근린 형태만큼 중요합니다.

align-navigation.title: ALIGN: Smart Navigation for Individual Preferences
align-navigation.overview:
Research Question

Can navigation apps personalize routes beyond distance/time? ALIGN generates routes meeting customized environmental criteria.

💡 Key Finding: ALIGN generates routes optimized for preferences like shade, safety, accessibility with only 8% distance penalty.

Preference Types
Route Generation

Current navigation ignores environmental quality. ALIGN incorporates spatially-resolved environmental data into routing.

Methodology

  • Data: Street-level tree, lighting, crime, accessibility data
  • Algorithm: Modified A* with environmental costs
  • Validation: User testing with diverse populations

Key Results

  1. Achieves Preferences: 90%+ user satisfaction
  2. Reasonable Trade-offs: Only 8% longer routes
  3. Accessibility: Valuable for wheelchair users, elderly

Implications

Enables accessible navigation and human-centered smart mobility systems.

🎯 Innovation

Pioneers environmentally-aware personalized navigation beyond time/distance.

spatial-modelling-forecasting.title: Spatial Modelling and Forecasting in Planning
spatial-modelling-forecasting.overview:
Research Question

How can planners use spatial modeling for evidence-based planning? This synthesizes approaches for understanding and predicting urban patterns.

💡 Key Finding: Integrating multiple spatial techniques - statistical, agent-based, machine learning - provides more robust insights than single approaches.

Application Domain
Planning Paradigm

Urban planning increasingly relies on quantitative analysis. This chapter guides method selection and interpretation.

Methodology

  • Survey: Comprehensive review of spatial modeling techniques
  • Classification: Organized by purpose (description, prediction, prescription)
  • Best Practices: Guidance on selection and validation

Key Content

  1. Statistical Models: Regression approaches
  2. Spatial Interaction: Gravity and accessibility models
  3. Agent-Based: Simulating individual behaviors
  4. Machine Learning: Pattern recognition in complex data

Implications

Adopt appropriate modeling tools and build organizational capacity for evidence-based planning.

🎯 Innovation

Comprehensive guidance on spatial modeling for planning practice and education.

pops-seoul.title: Ground Floor Facilities and POPS in Seoul
pops-seoul.overview:
Research Question

How do ground floor facilities influence use of Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS)? This examines whether nearby uses affect public space activation.

💡 Key Finding: POPS near food/beverage and retail show 3-4x higher usage. Ground floor use is critical but overlooked for public space success.

Sample Size
Outcome Measure

POPS provide public amenities in exchange for development bonuses, but many remain underused. This investigates surrounding uses.

Methodology

  • Observation: Systematic usage counts at different times
  • Ground Floor Survey: Detailed inventory of uses within 50m
  • Analysis: Regression predicting usage from land use composition

Key Results

  1. Food/Beverage Critical: 3-4x higher usage near cafes/restaurants
  2. Retail Important: Shops increase activation
  3. Office Insufficient: Office-only surroundings = low usage
  4. Mix Optimal: Diversity creates most vibrant spaces

Implications

Regulate ground floor uses surrounding POPS and coordinate public space with ground floor planning.

🎯 Innovation

Highlights critical role of surrounding ground floor uses in public space activation.
